body:
## Summary

Fixes #2144.

A `solve https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/927 --auto-merge` run stopped after its first monitoring iteration with:

```
❌ GITHUB TARGET UNAVAILABLE: Issue #905 has been closed.
   Action:                 Stopping auto-restart-until-mergeable mode
```

…in the **same** probe that reported the pull request as `"state":"open", "mergeable":true, "mergeable_state":"clean"`. Nothing was posted to GitHub and the process exited `0`, so the run looked successful while the pull request sat unmerged. A human merged it manually two hours later (`merged_at: 2026-08-06T09:51:10Z`).

## Root cause

`src/github-terminal-state.lib.mjs` was written for #1931, where the problem was the opposite one — a deleted repository made the watcher sleep forever. It therefore treated *every* missing-or-closed entity as terminal, including the linked issue. But closing an issue is the normal end state of solved work; it says nothing about whether the pull request can be merged.

Two further defects were found while investigating:

- **Every stop path was silent.** The issue is explicit about this: *"in any case when our process is stopped … we should comment that we stopped and exactly why. At the moment there is no GitHub comments in that cases."*
- **The quiet probes from #2130 were defeated.** All three callers injected their own mirroring `$` into `checkGitHubTerminalState`, overriding its quiet default runner, so ~33 KB of pull request JSON plus the full issue payload were written to the attached log on every iteration (log lines 11419-11420).

## Changes

- `src/github-terminal-state.lib.mjs` now returns **merge blockers** in addition to terminal states. A closed or deleted **issue** is a merge blocker: the loop keeps making the pull request mergeable. The only terminal states left are pull-request-scoped (merged/closed/unreachable, missing branches) or repository-scoped.
- A closed issue holds back `--auto-merge` **only**. When it does, the tool comments that the pull request is ready and asks the user to reopen the issue or merge it manually.
- New `src/automation-stop-reporting.lib.mjs`: a registry of 13 stop reasons — each with a title, an explanation and concrete next steps — plus comment builders and a deduped, never-throwing reporter. Wired into all **11** stop paths across `--auto-merge`, `--auto-restart-until-mergeable` and `--watch`. An unknown reason code degrades to a generic comment, so a new stop can never regress to silence.
- `attemptAutoMerge` extracted into `src/solve.auto-merge-attempt.lib.mjs` to stay inside the repository's 1500-line file policy.
- All three callers now pass `commandRunner: quietProbe($)`.

## How to reproduce

```bash
node experiments/issue-2144/repro-closed-issue-stops-loop.mjs
```

It replays the exact GitHub state from the incident and exits non-zero if a closed linked issue stops the loop again. It also prints the two comments the tool now publishes.

## Tests

- `tests/test-closed-issue-merge-blocking-2144.mjs` — **new**, 19 assertions: terminal-state classification (closed issue, deleted issue, open issue, closed PR, merged PR, deleted repo, deleted branch, `issueNumber === prNumber`), comment bodies, reporter behaviour (dedup, unavailable targets, never throws), and call-site wiring.
- `tests/test-github-terminal-state-1931.mjs` — the closed-issue case is inverted to the new intended behaviour, with a comment pointing at this issue.
- `tests/test-issue-2130-log-noise.mjs` — new case: no caller may pass a mirroring `$` to the terminal-state probe.
- `tests/test-auto-delete-branch-on-merge-401.mjs` — updated to look at both auto-merge call paths, one of which moved into the extracted module.

## Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-2144/README.md` — the incident timeline (with log line numbers), the full requirement inventory, the three root causes, an edge-case matrix, the codebase sweep, and the components considered. Raw data (the 11 518-line log and `gh api` snapshots of the pull request and both issues) is under `docs/case-studies/issue-2144/data/`.

Two things are documented but deliberately unchanged: `solve` still exits `0` after a stop (changing that would change the contract `hive` relies on), and `src/hive.recheck.lib.mjs` still skips closed issues when selecting *new* work, which is correct.

commits.messageBody:
Adding .gitkeep for PR creation (default mode).
This file will be removed when the task is complete.

Issue: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2144

A closed linked issue was classified as a terminal state, so
--auto-restart-until-mergeable stopped on the very first check of an open,
mergeable pull request -- and stopped without posting any GitHub comment.

- github-terminal-state.lib.mjs: issue-scoped states (closed / inaccessible)
  are demoted from terminal to non-terminal `mergeBlockers`. Only pull
  request, repository and branch losses still stop the loop.
- automation-stop-reporting.lib.mjs (new): a registry of every stop reason
  plus `reportAutomationStop`, so each stop path publishes exactly why it
  stopped, deduplicated and tracked as a tool comment.
- solve.auto-merge.lib.mjs / solve.watch.lib.mjs: every stop path now reports;
  issue blockers gate only the final merge.
- solve.auto-merge-attempt.lib.mjs (new): `attemptAutoMerge` extracted to keep
  both files under the 1500-line limit.

Tests: tests/test-closed-issue-merge-blocking-2144.mjs (19 cases) and an
inverted assertion in tests/test-github-terminal-state-1931.mjs.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(2144): closed issues block only auto-merge, never the mergeable loop

commits.messageBody:
Issue #2130 made checkGitHubTerminalState's default runner quiet, but all
three callers injected their own mirroring $, which overrode it. The
incident log for this issue still carried the full repository, pull request,
branch and issue payloads once per watch iteration. Bind quietProbe($)
instead and add a regression test.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(2144): keep terminal-state probes quiet in every caller

auto-delete-branch test, whose second call path moved into the extracted
solve.auto-merge-attempt module.
